chapter: 1977: Kansas City honor and the piano
title: Sonny Greer, drums and the organ on his recent albums
summary: Basie says the organ on a Pablo record was a throw-in and that he plays it at home to relax and imagine the orchestra.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: But I do want to get on this since
it's in print already and I found that Nat Shapiro had written about you in an earlier tape that we did here about --
Who?
Nat Shapiro. He wrote about you. remember when we were talking, so it's in print, so it's nothing new. When Sonny Greer took you from the drums, is that right?
Yeah.
Okay, so let's talk about how you played piano -- I mean, drums -- How about organ?
That's something for my amusement only, actually.
But you played it on your album with Oscar.
Well, that consists of only a throw-in, a little background.
"Satch and Josh" that you just did for (inaudible) Pablo.
I didn't request it at all.
You mean it was Norman's idea.
You just happened to have an organ there.
Yeah.
So you just sat down and did it.

I like the organ so well. I wish I could do a lot of things on it. Recordwise. I would really do that if I really thought I could do it successfully. To me, I hadn't thought about even doing it (inaudible) to relax myself with it and play just for me.
So in other words, if there was an
organ some place and you had the recording equipment and somebody set up a recording, you could do that.

No, I don't think so, because there would be too many stops in it. Especially when I play at home, I do quite a bit of thinking, thinking of different moods and things that I would like to hear the orchestra.
In other words, you'd be thinking of the orchestra.
Yes, I think a lot of things, and that I can really do. The arrangers that I got now, something I heard.
